blocks.text: Chicken, Egg, and Turkey Farms in Canada's Poultry Capital

parts.t: Abbotsford is home to the highest concentration of supply-managed poultry farms in British Columbia, supported by local processors, feed mills on Sumas Way and Railway Street, specialized poultry veterinarians, and barn equipment contractors across Sumas Prairie, Matsqui Prairie, Bradner, Aberdeen, and South Poplar. Because of that agricultural infrastructure, commercial broiler chicken, table-egg layer, broiler hatching egg, and turkey farms in Abbotsford consistently command strong demand from both expanding Fraser Valley farm families and new entrants.

When evaluating an Abbotsford poultry farm, commercial value is driven primarily by two assets beyond the ALR land and residence: (1) the production quota issued under supply management by the BC Chicken Marketing Board, BC Egg Marketing Board, BC Broiler Hatching Egg Commission, or BC Turkey Marketing Board; and (2) the physical poultry barns—specifically single-storey vs double-decker construction, clear-span trusses, ventilation and computer environmental controls, standby diesel generators, biosecurity fencing, manure storage, and water treatment systems.

blocks.text: How Poultry Quota Transfers and Off-Market Sales Work in Abbotsford

parts.t: Quota does not automatically run with the land title in British Columbia. For an Abbotsford poultry farm sale to include production quota, the Contract of Purchase and Sale must explicitly specify the exact volume of quota being transferred (e.g., kilograms of live weight per 8-week cycle for broiler chickens, or layer bird housing capacity), and both buyer and seller must apply for marketing-board transfer approval and premises certification prior to completion. Many MLS® poultry listings are marketed as land and barns only (where the seller has relocated or sold quota separately, leaving barns suited to quota leasing, new-entrant programs, specialty poultry, or agricultural storage), while many going-concern quota farms trade confidentially off-market among pre-qualified agricultural buyers.

blocks.text: 7 Common Questions About Abbotsford Poultry Farms

parts.t: What makes Abbotsford poultry farms valuable compared to other BC regions?

Abbotsford has the deepest poultry infrastructure in Western Canada—with major feed mills, processors, hatcheries, poultry veterinarians, and barn service technicians minutes away—which lowers operating costs and supports strong resale liquidity for barns and land.
Is production quota included when I buy an Abbotsford poultry farm on the MLS®?

Only if explicitly stated in the listing and the Contract of Purchase and Sale. Quota does not run with the land title; many MLS® farm listings offer the ALR land, residence, and poultry barns without quota, while going-concern sales specify exact quota units and require marketing-board transfer approval.
Which marketing boards govern poultry farms in Abbotsford?

Depending on the sector, operations are regulated by the BC Chicken Marketing Board (broilers, roasters, specialty chicken), BC Egg Marketing Board (table layers), BC Broiler Hatching Egg Commission, or BC Turkey Marketing Board.
What should I inspect on the poultry barns before removing subjects?

Inspect barn dimensions and square footage per deck, structural wood trusses and concrete floors, ventilation fans and environmental controllers, feed lines and water nipple systems, backup power generator capacity, biosecurity gate layout, and the farm's BC premises ID and certification status.
Which Abbotsford sub-areas have the most poultry farms?

Poultry operations are heavily concentrated across Sumas Prairie, Matsqui Prairie, Bradner, Aberdeen, and South Poplar—all located inside the Agricultural Land Reserve (A2 zoning) with truck access to Highway 1 and Highway 11.
What floodplain and environmental rules apply to Abbotsford poultry farms?

Farms on Sumas Prairie and Matsqui Prairie sit inside the City of Abbotsford Floodplain Development Permit Area (governing Flood Construction Levels for new barns and houses) and must comply with the BC Code of Practice for Agricultural Environmental Management regarding nutrient and manure handling.
How do I buy or value an off-market poultry farm in Abbotsford?

In an established poultry hub like Abbotsford, many going-concern chicken and egg farms sell privately. Call or text Jared Gibbons at 604-928-1361 or email jared@jaredgibbons.ca for confidential off-market opportunities and farm valuations.
